## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Virāgakathā* ("Discussion of Dispassion", Ps 2.5) is a chapter of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* within the Pali canonical collection [SuttaCentral]. The text sets out analytical expositions concerning the nature and realization of dispassion (*virāga*), framing path factors in relation to dispassion and liberation; for example, it correlates the spiritual path by defining the "dispassion of seeing" as right view (*dassana-virāgo sammā-diṭṭhi*) and the "freedom of seeing" as right view (*dassana-vimutti sammā-diṭṭhi*) [Gethin 2001]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analyses conducted by DharmaNexus show widespread internal parallels across 43 Pali texts, comprising over 1,300 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, the *Virāgakathā* shares substantial textual material with the *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), *Maggakathā* (Ps 1.9), *Abhisamayakathā* (Ps 3.3), *Indriyakathā* (Ps 1.4), *Ānāpānassatikathā* (Ps 1.3), *Bojjhaṅgakathā* (Ps 2.3), *Maṇḍapeyyakathā* (Ps 1.10), *Vimokkhakathā* (Ps 1.5), and *Yuganaddhakathā* (Ps 2.1), as well as the *Jhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 34) of the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* [DharmaNexus]. Heavy textual sharing also connects it to post-canonical exegetical works, prominently the *Visuddhimagga*, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā*, and the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language comparisons, DharmaNexus aligns passages from the *Virāgakathā* with Buddhist Sanskrit works such as the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, along with Tibetan translations including the *Āryadaśabhūmivyākhyāna* (D3993) and the *Gaganagañjaparipṛcchāsūtra* (D0148) [DharmaNexus].
